title: Bleaching the rainbow
text: Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor yet {{1}} about a quarter of all marine species. Their foundation is a partnership: the coral animal builds the {{2}}, and microscopic algae living inside its tissues supply most of its food through photosynthesis, in exchange for shelter. When the water stays too warm, this partnership {{3}}. Stressed corals expel their algae, and the transparent animal shows the white skeleton beneath — a ghostly colour that gives bleaching its name. Bleached coral is not dead, and a quick return to cooler water lets it {{4}}; repeated or prolonged heat, however, starves it, and whole reefs have turned to rubble within a decade. The scale is now {{5}}: mass bleaching events that were once a once-in-a-century anomaly strike the Great Barrier Reef repeatedly. Scientists are therefore {{6}} the hard questions: selecting heat-tolerant strains of algae, breeding corals that {{7}} warmer water, and shading trials that sound desperate but buy time. None of it {{8}} the underlying cause, of course — only emissions cuts can do that — but reef science has entered the pragmatic age: save what can be saved, and learn from what cannot.

gaps.explanation: 'support about a quarter of marine species' — provide the habitat they need; supply would mean handing species out, which is not what a reef does.
'builds the structure' — the reef's physical frame; fracture = a crack, nurture = care.
'this partnership collapses' — breaks down entirely; collude = conspire, convene = meet.
'lets it recover' — return to health; recoil = draw back in fear, recount = tell again.
'the scale is now unprecedented' — it has no precedent, matching the once-a-century events now repeating; unpredictable means impossible to forecast, which is not the point.
'scientists are tackling the hard questions' — taking them on; tickle = touch lightly, trample = crush underfoot.
'corals that withstand warmer water' — endure it without harm; withhold = refuse to give, withdraw = take back.
'none of it addresses the underlying cause' — tackles it directly; attest = provide evidence of, adorn = decorate.
